nodes.label: CRM Program
nodes.rationale: People, processes and technologies a business deploys to increase customer focus; success requires more than buying software.

nodes.label: Data-Driven Learning Organization
nodes.rationale: Reports and dashboards act as instrumentation: you can't manage what you can't measure.

nodes.label: Organizational Change Preparation
nodes.rationale: Change meets resistance; data-driven culture, executive support, communication, training, feedback and recognition reduce it.

nodes.label: Four Pillars of CRM Success
nodes.rationale: Success rests on people, process, technology and reasonable expectations.

nodes.label: Executive Sponsor
nodes.rationale: Must be a CRM believer from the customer-facing side, not finance or IT.

nodes.label: Subject-Matter Experts
nodes.rationale: Include front-line doers; executives alone misjudge how work actually happens.

nodes.label: Closed-Loop Marketing Attribution
nodes.rationale: Tie marketing spend to sales results so funds go to programs that produce revenue.

nodes.label: Customer ID Crosswalk
nodes.rationale: Disparate systems need a mapping table so Account #245 in accounting equals Customer #8879 in marketing.

nodes.label: Customer Self-Service Portal
nodes.rationale: Developed after structured issue tracking and a seeded knowledge base.

nodes.label: Change Control Process
nodes.rationale: Interconnected CRM touches all groups, so uncontrolled changes cause chaos; standing review meeting plus minor release schedule.

nodes.label: CRM Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Living 1-3 year plan aligning CRM initiatives with strategic goals.

nodes.label: Software-as-a-Service
nodes.rationale: Predictable cost and no infrastructure burden, but higher lifetime cost and vendor lock-in.

nodes.label: Dev Test Production Environments
nodes.rationale: Never develop in production; testers need stable environments; refresh from production and migrate components through gates.

nodes.label: Passive vs Active CRM
nodes.rationale: Without workflow, CRM is an electronic filing cabinet; workflow on events makes it an active participant.

nodes.label: User Adoption
nodes.rationale: Poor user experience has doomed more CRM initiatives than any other factor; abandonment feeds back on itself.

nodes.label: Big Bang vs Phased Approach
nodes.rationale: Phased projects deliver value sooner, allow lessons learned, and reduce risk; big bang collapses under its own weight.

nodes.label: Total Cost of Ownership
nodes.rationale: ROI analysis for CRM selection is rarely credible; prefer TCO over 5-7 years.

nodes.label: Iterative and Incremental Development
nodes.rationale: Recommended: overlapping stages and repeated design/build loops put the application in front of users early for buy-in.

nodes.label: Over-customization
nodes.rationale: Too many fields/automations cause user confusion, process impacts and extra support cost; control via iterative reviews and scope tools.

nodes.label: Success Criteria
nodes.rationale: Clearly documented success criteria let you articulate CRM value post-deployment and secure funding for future phases.

nodes.label: Use Case Definition
nodes.rationale: Use cases align process discussions and provide a baseline for complete testing against approved design rather than what was built.

nodes.label: Custom Development
nodes.rationale: Valuable but risky: cost, upgrade path, IT resources, vendor roadmap, ISV alternatives must be weighed; prefer off-the-shelf ISV add-ons when equal.

nodes.label: Data-Level Integration
nodes.rationale: Copies data so it participates fully in CRM reports, workflow, security; costlier to build. Requires deciding data flow direction and system of record.

nodes.label: User Interface Integration
nodes.rationale: Embeds a view of another app's data; simpler but data cannot be searched or used in CRM workflow.

nodes.label: Unique Identifiers / ID Crosswalk
nodes.rationale: Names are not enough to link records across systems; store the other system's unique ID or maintain a separate identifier table.

nodes.label: KPI Principles
nodes.rationale: Specific, owned, measurable, timely, limited in number, with targets, aligned to organizational goals.

nodes.label: Data Warehouse
nodes.rationale: Enables time-series trends, multi-source data and avoids load on CRM, at the cost of extra complexity and non-real-time data.

nodes.label: Data Migration
nodes.rationale: Difficult, expensive and imprecise; default to not migrating unless business value justifies it. Garbage in, garbage out.

nodes.label: User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
nodes.rationale: Executed by business users to validate the app supports business process; cannot be outsourced to the consulting partner.

nodes.label: Software-Driven Projects
nodes.rationale: Letting tool features drive process risks adoption; mold the tool to the business process.

Service maturity path: issue tracking, knowledge base, self-service
